scenes.heading: Hiring your first employee or subcontractor

sents.d: Hiring your first employee or subcontractor
Growth beyond your own capacity usually requires bringing on help.

scenes.heading: Hire when you're turning work away

sents.d: The clearest signal it's time to hire is consistently turning away work or being fully booked weeks out — hiring before that point risks not having enough work to sustain a second person's pay.
Understanding the legal distinction between an employee and an independent contractor in your area matters, since misclassifying workers can create significant tax and legal liability later.
Starting with a trial period or a smaller number of jobs before fully relying on a new hire lets you assess quality and reliability with lower risk than immediately handing over a full workload.

take: Hire once you're consistently booked out, and classify workers correctly.
